sense.text:
“And of the twelve prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place.” These are the twelve, and they come back in the last days. Every time they come back, their job is the same: “for they comforted Jacob.” To comfort Jacob is to comfort us, the children of Israel, in this life, because we are in the last days and going into some hard times, and Satan is not playing with any of us.

“And delivered them by assured hope.” That is what this class is about: the power of hope. The prophets deliver Jacob by an assured hope, and that hope is for the salvation to come.

Look at the movement in place right now: brothers going out to every city in the Northeast on the migrant blitz, reaching the scattered of Israel throughout the four corners of the earth, the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom, as Isaiah 11 speaks of. It is a serious mission, and you are part of a great thing in this earth. That is why you have to shake the boy spirit and become men.

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” This is how the prophets comfort Jacob: through the scriptures. That is where our hope is going to be, brothers.

In these scriptures they comfort us by showing us that we are the children of Israel; showing us why Christ died, and what we did to allow our King to die for us; whether Christ died for all nations; that Christ is a black man; and whether the children of Israel are all colours of people. Right now we are in the last days, in Babylon, where the children of Israel are made to look like the Edomite. Throughout their history it has always been a fight between the children of Jacob and the Edomite, so how did the Edomite become us in the last days?

We are in captivity, fathers and mothers, and we must understand that. The comfort and the hope come out of the scriptures.

sense.text:
“As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help: in our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us.” We put our hope in America, thinking America was going to save us, because of their welfare, their housing, their jobs. That is vain help. America cannot even help herself, for her debt reaches into heaven. That is an unjust place, a wicked place.

We look at the white man as though he is just. The white man is not just, never has been, never will be. Look at the arrogance of this place: the father Bush said he would never apologize for the United States, whatever the facts, after his government shot down a civilian plane full of Iranians; the son made an unjust war on Iraq, then said himself, mixing up Iraq and Ukraine, that it was an unjustified and brutal invasion. They killed a million people in Iraq, and more than that, and destabilized the Middle East on a lie, and nobody came to apologize. From the father to the son they are criminal people; they are demons. All of them think the same; don't be a fool. Their wealth was taken by genocide of the native peoples, theft of land, and the slave trade.

When the Lord speaks of them that destroy the earth, it is talking about them: look at the bombs dropped in Gaza and in Africa and throughout the world, and their effect on people to this day. We are in the most evil place on this planet. Paul said we live by faith, not by sight: don't believe what you see on the TV.

When they asked Malcolm X whether the black man would fight for America against Russia or China, he answered that we will fight for the souls of our people. Our people fought for America ever since there was an America and came home to heroin, drugs, guns and murder, not gold and silver. Now we are awake: we will not fight for America; we will pray for the destruction of America. When you see us marching throughout the earth, it is not a regular march. We are fighting for the souls of our people, for the hope of our people, before the Lord brings destruction on America.

precepts.why:
“That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro”. When we were tossed to and fro, people used us. America was sold to us as a land of milk and honey, and we found out America is a nightmare to our people. We did not know where we were.

“And carried about with every wind of doctrine”: because we wanted to be part of this system, we jumped on any philosophy put on us. They gave us Christianity, we jumped on it; they gave us religion, Islam, we jumped on it, not realizing that we are the sons of the living God.

Now we are wide awake. We have to keep the sabbath days, the feast days and the new moons: these are the works of the Most High that we have to keep in these last days. We are not out here to celebrate Christmas, Thanksgiving, Mother's Day and Father's Day. That was when we were dead in our sin.

sense.text:
They tell us to fight for America against the Chinese and the Russians. What has America done for us as a people? Look how many of our brothers are in jail, how many of our people are on drugs, what has been done in the black community. If you are blind, just go and look.

“Awake to righteousness, and sin not”. That is what we must do. When we awake, we have to understand that we can no longer sin, because we were dead: we were in a state of death because of sin, and now we are awake.

“For some have not the knowledge of God: I speak this to your shame.” We are supposed to have the knowledge of God, but some of us do not, and he speaks that to our shame, because the knowledge of God was given to the children of Israel. How could we lack it? We have to take heed, brothers, and understand that this place is going to destroy a lot of us if we do not take heed to these commandments.

precepts.why: “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge”. That is what God said: we are destroyed for a lack of knowledge. It is the knowledge of God that 1 Corinthians 15:34 says some of us do not have, to our shame, and the lack of it is our destruction.

What is the knowledge? “The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted of him, and wisdom obtaineth his love.” Then: “The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life”.

The knowledge of God that we lack is the knowledge of his commandments, and that is the doctrine we are supposed to live by.

“For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The good doctrine is for us not to forsake God's laws. That is God's knowledge.

We have to understand, families, that we can no longer play a game with our life. Now that we are awake to righteousness, there are things we must do.

sense.text:
“For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”. Within the mind of men proceed evil thoughts: adultery, fornication and all the rest. Now we understand what is going on in the black community.

This is how powerful Satan is in his kingdom. A thought travels in about a quarter of a second, and as soon as that information goes in, it affects you physically and mentally. Some of you watch porn and do not know how demonic it is: the thought of it alone affects your studying, your learning, your meditating in these laws and your fasting. And the white man uses the speed of the thought against us.

The first thing you must take control over, as you wake up in this truth, is your mind, and you must guard it with all diligence, because that is where thoughts and imagination come from. The emotional side of the mind cannot reason; it deals with feelings. God does not deal with your feelings and emotions; God deals with fact and common sense.

When we come to repentance we must take full control of the mind. If you take full control of your mind, would you feed it with anything? That is why God said to meditate on these things day and night. There is a reason behind it.

“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” They come from within men, and they defile the man. Was not Adam defiled because that thought was already in there? So we have to understand what we have to control: the mind.
“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” If you come to serve the Lord, you have to prepare your soul for temptation.

“Set thy heart aright”: set your mind aright. “And constantly endure”: that is the key. Use the word in a sentence: the world is constantly changing. Should we be like the world? No. The Lord wants us to constantly endure; we have to fight.

To set your heart aright is to take full control of your mind. Treat your mind like a little baby, like your son or your daughter: mind, I heard what you said, but sit down; we are not going to entertain that right now. We used to do that, but we are not going to do that now. If you used to love little children, if you used to watch a lot of porn, whatever lifestyle you came from, you have to endure that thought. You can no longer flip-flop in and out, because we see the last days and the wars; we are already in the mix of the third war.

If you find yourself more within yourself than in the brotherhood, something is wrong with you. Don't fool yourself that you had a headache or a runny nose and that is why you did not come to class. That is playing games, not constantly enduring, and that kind is going to be in the lake of fire soon.

precepts.why:
“For the thoughts of mortal men are miserable, and our devices are but uncertain.” We have miserable thoughts; we have a miserable mind.

“For the corruptible body presseth down the soul”: the corruptible body we are in right now. See what we are fighting against: ourselves. People say easily that a brother made them sin or a sister made them sin, but that is not the case. Sometimes we are fighting against our own lust.

“And the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” The mind that museth upon many things can hardly think right and can hardly be controlled. But we are learning; we have to take full control of it. We cannot sleep on the mind, because that is where we find ourselves defiled. Within the mind a lot is going on, a constant fight, and that is why we must set the heart aright.

Some of us do not think we can overcome anything, but you can overcome anything, as long as you are living in these commandments. Some people see our shortcomings, but they have not seen our perfection yet; they are going to.

“This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly”. We have to affirm it constantly, “that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works.” Satan is at work, and our mind is against us, so we have to constantly maintain the good works and take full control.

That is why we have to constantly ask each other: brother, did you read your four chapters today? Sister, did you watch the captain's class, the bishop's class, anything today? If you are not watching these things, you are entertaining something else; remember how fast the thoughts are. And when the Bible is not open between a brother and a sister talking in a corner for an hour or two, it is always going to be gossip.

Satan attacked Job through his children and his wealth, and Job's wife said, Curse God and die, and Job checked her: all this time we lived a good life and never heard curse God; good comes with evil, and you speak like a foolish woman. Because she was checked, the Lord was able to bless Job at the end with new children and new wealth. Not every wealth is good.

sense.text:
“Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands”. Our minds can be fearful. Now that Trump is in power, a brother might say, I don't know where I stand, I don't know if I can do this or that. God says woe to the fearful heart, because our hearts and minds have to be in him. Whatever a brother sees in society, he has to shake that fear off.

The ICE they have set up is the same as the Ku Klux Klan of the sixties. Don't think they are regular people. The Klan was part of the government, and the government said, that's not us, it's just the Klan. Don't be a fool.

“Woe unto him that is fainthearted! for he believeth not”. If your heart is faint, the Lord says woe, destruction, because a fearful heart does not believe. No matter what your eyes or the news are telling you, put your trust in the Lord. If any of us go to jail for what we preach, so be it. You are connected to this world, afraid of death and of the government, because your faith is not strong yet. Wherever we find ourselves, in jail or back where we came from, we have to learn to push harder.

“Therefore shall he not be defended.” Because you believe not, you will not be defended in that day. Today you are in Islam, tomorrow in Christianity, the next day in meditation with the Chinese or healing stones, when you used to know that God's commandments heal all things. That is a mind that is offended, a mind with no patience.
“Woe unto you that have lost patience! and what will ye do when the Lord shall visit you?” When the Lord returns, a heart that is offended and has no patience will be destroyed, put to death.

“They that fear the Lord will not disobey his Word”. When you fear God, you understand constantly enduring and patience, and you understand that we are marked for death for what we are pushing through the earth. Since you know you are marked for death, what are you worried about? Tie up your boots and go do something.

“And they that love him will keep his ways.” That brother or sister understands what temptation is. They will not hang out with friends who smoke weed or sniff coke, or with gang members, because in the mix of their wickedness anything can happen. Hang with the righteous and you will be all right; hang with the wicked and you will be touched.

“They that fear the Lord will seek that which is well, pleasing unto him”. What pleases the Lord? Going to jail, being put to death, going through your affliction for this truth: that is well pleasing to the Lord, because it is already written. Paul went through it, the apostles went through it, Christ went through it, the prophets went through it. Who are you? Wake up.

“And they that love him shall be filled with the law.” If you love the Lord, you will be filled with God's laws, and God will defend you, dead or alive, in jail or not, in affliction or not. That is why you have to build your character and your spirit, because the flesh is weak. When a brother is put to death for wearing fringes, the thought comes, use wisdom, my brother: is that the right thought? That is well pleasing to the Lord.

“They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts”: that is the fresh water. We prepare our heart for death and for the unjust thoughts that will trouble us in this life. Shake off the sabbath sickness and the feast day flu.

“And humble their souls in his sight”. When you fear the Lord, you prepare your heart to humble your soul in the presence of God, and you will not disobey his words. Fasting is a form of humbleness; praying is a form of humbleness; taking heed to what the leaders said and perfecting it is a form of humbleness.

Ask yourself: are you in this truth to perfect yourself, or to play games? If you are here to perfect it, you will meditate on these things day and night; if not, you will have an excuse for everything. Nine or ten years in the truth and still a soldier or an officer of ten: nobody holds you back but your sin, the gossip, the complaining, the bitterness. God does the promoting. A brother once wondered why he was not raised up to captain, and it came out that he was fighting homosexuality within him, in the mix of his sin; asked which one he was, he said, I'm the receiver. You want to be a captain and you never killed that demon? This is a spiritual war, and we can see beyond and read your mind. You cannot be a leader over men while you never fight what is inside you.

“Judge not, that ye be not judged.” A lot of our people do not understand that. That is why we constantly have to pray for forgiveness: a lot of us want to judge brothers and sisters while we ourselves are not right.

“For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.” Be very mindful when you judge. If you judge with mercy, the same mercy will reach out to you; if you judge with cruelty, when your judgment comes, there will be cruelty too.

“And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye”: some brothers and sisters can see someone else's sin clearly. “But considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?” We have to consider the beam in our own eye, the sin we do not acknowledge, which keeps us from judging right. That is why we have to judge with mercy.

A brother condemns a brother for watching porn, and the night before he was watching a movie with naked things in it, and told himself it was just the movie. The thought goes by in a second and you deceive your mind. How can you judge the brother that watches porn while you love movies that are half porn? Consider yourself.

“Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye?” In the Maccabees we learned that sport is not for our people, but some brothers watch every season of baseball, football and basketball and know every star, and say, my faith is strong. That is not strong faith. A sister will go to a Chris Brown concert wearing fringes. Imagine a shootout at that concert, and a deacon, a captain, an officer and sisters are among the dead: would that look good for us? The same idol you worshipped in the world, the same music, you are still serving in Christ. Don't let Satan deceive you. Know your beam; know your sin.

Bishop told of a brother who had just condemned another brother for watching porn, then went to show the Bishop something on his phone, and porn popped up. You can be just in the eyes of men, but you want to be just in the eyes of God, because the flesh easily deceives us into believing we are in this truth.

“Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.” Paul said, examine yourself, to see if you are in the faith. One year, two years, nine, ten, eleven years in the truth and not growing: examine yourself. Go inside your mind, like the man in the film Incarnate who went inside his clients' minds to find when the demon came in. Find when your weakness came in: the demon of fatigue against God's law and God's work. Every man knows his weakness. Meditation is going inside the mind, five or ten minutes, and removing whatever stops you from growing. If you lack zeal for study, pray: Lord, give me the first zeal I had when I first knew I was Israel.

“For every one that asketh receiveth”. If you ask for wisdom you will receive it, but wisdom is not a spirit that just jumps on you. God puts you in the environment of wisdom: being around like-minded brothers who have the wisdom, so that it spreads to you. A brother who will not come to the table for wisdom thinks he already has his own, and then he is confused by a simple question, like the difference between Christ and an animal sacrifice.

“And he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.” When we first came in, we never had a day off. Brothers took a three-hour train to class, stayed till four or five in the morning with work the next day; brothers met on Friday nights and on weekday classes. We were knocking because we saw these men as men of wisdom. When you get knocked down, get up again and keep knocking. The Bishop made a book, a fifty-page timeline of Syria, Babylon, Persia, Greece and Rome, for the real disciples, and brothers given it have not read past page 12. We will not be around each other much longer; while we have the Bishop and deacons, learn as much as possible, because millions of our people need to be saved.

precepts.why:
“Study to shew thyself approved unto God”. We are not knocking you for no reason: the scripture tells you to study to show yourself approved. “A workman that needeth not to be ashamed”: if you are a workman, you have to study not to be ashamed. If you are not growing in the spirit, examine it: when you teach in the street and your voice is soft, you have to come with more power and make your voice heard, the way singers train their voice. You are a mighty man in this earth; act like it. Sitting alone in front of a computer, not out teaching anybody, is a weak spirit.

“Rightly dividing the word of truth.” We have to rightly divide the word of truth.

sense.text:
“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation”. That is the man that constantly endures: he is constantly fighting within himself and taking full control of his mind. When you constantly endure, you do not give only 10% of yourself; you give all you have. Give 10% and you look like the 10%; give 20% and you look like the 20%. Push yourself to the limit, like the brothers in the scriptures who were sick for the gospel's sake and kept on pushing.

Recognize your position. An officer of twenty whose friends are only the tens and the soldiers is not growing. An officer of ten is a high position: guiding your own self through the week is hard enough, and now ten men. An officer of ten who talks to one brother all week, an officer of twenty who talks to two, an officer of fifty who talks to one brother the whole week before the sabbath: he is full of bovine excrement. Many barely talk to the brothers and only do the work when called and told to do it. An officer of twenty who is already doing the work of an eighty or a fifty, you will see it in his works; you do not have to chase him. But the brother who will not do the work of a fifty and still says, you better promote me, I deserve it: that mind is a wicked mind.

precepts.why:
For brothers who want to be officers and captains: “And if thou seest a man of understanding, get thee betimes unto him”. Get next to a brother of understanding. If you are a soldier, get with an officer of ten or twenty; ask him how he came up the ranks. “And let thy foot wear the steps of his door”: get next to him constantly and ask questions. There are no dumb questions. That is how you learn and build yourself up.

“Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord”, not on sports and not on porn: those are distractions. “And meditate continually in his commandments”: that takes time. “He shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine owns desire.” Then you will be established, recognized and sought after for your wisdom, and raised up as an officer or a captain.

How many brothers call during the week? Very rarely. You have to constantly endure, and cast out the thought that tells you that you are okay in the condition you are in.

“They shall fear thee as long as the sun and moon endure, throughout all generations.” The sun and moon endure because they have work to do. You never see the moon or the sun get up and say, I'm going to take the day off.

So we do not take days off. Push yourself regardless. Connecticut will be better with you or without you, but we have to do better: by the time summer comes we have to do greater than last year.

“For the Lord is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.” You do not see God's truth taking a day off. It endures to every generation; it does not stop; it keeps promoting itself to every generation.

Likewise you have to promote yourself every year and do better. The little you have, be the best at it.

“His work is honourable and glorious: and his righteousness endureth for ever.” God's righteousness does not just hang around; it endures for ever, and when we operate within his righteousness, we have no days off.

Our people are sick out there and need watches in every community; they need God's commandments, and that is what the blitz is about. Some of you do only two blitzes a year, only the local ones. Repent of that spirit and shake that dust.

sense.text:
“So that we ourselves glory in you in the churches of God for your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that ye endure”. We glory in you for your patience. That is what these classes are about: to endure, because our people need us out there. In your patience you possess your soul.

We are in a job of enduring. If you find yourself in jail, endure. Afflicted, endure. Put to death, endure. If they raid your house for Christ's sake and take your stuff, endure: you can buy those things again. The key is to endure.

precepts.why:
“He that shall endure the peril in that time hath kept himself: they that be fallen into danger are such as have works, and faith toward the Almighty.” The brothers who fall into danger are the brothers who put the work in, who have faith toward God and faith in Christ and keep pushing no matter what.

That is what to get out of these classes: there will be hard times and perilous times, but if you remember nothing else, keep it pushing.

“And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith, whereby ye have believed”. The brothers who put their works in are the ones who will escape in these last days, because they keep it pushing by faith.

We were given a job to do. The duty of all men on earth is to fear God and keep his commandments, and if you fear God and keep his commandments, you will push his commandments throughout the earth. Your little job is temporary before the white man takes it away. Brothers who wanted wisdom, the ones who became captains, were everywhere the brothers were. Whatever your rank, if you think you have it already, think again.

sense.text:
“Let all things be performed after the law of God”: let everything you do be performed after the laws of God. “Diligently”. Ask yourself, are you diligent? The job you signed up for, can the brothers count on you, can the sisters count on you? You claim to be the wife of a captain or an officer and do a little work, and during the week you only talk to those you gossip with instead of building up the sisters. Some brothers gossip too. Check that spirit.

“Unto the most high God”. If you are diligent unto the most high God, it becomes natural to you, and wisdom knows her children.

“That they might set their hope in God”. These brothers and sisters put their hope in God; that is our job, to put our hope in God. Remember the class: the power of hope. That is our joy, to have our hope in the Lord.

“And not forget the works of God”. When you put your trust in God, you do not forget the work of God; you push diligently. You say you trust God: are you diligent and honest in his work? Isaiah 11 is an open door, and some do not even have a passport.

“But keep his commandments”. The work of God is to keep his commandments, and that is what we spread throughout the world. We will not forget the works of God, because our people depend on us. That is the type of man and the type of system we are trying to build.

precepts.why:
The prophets think the same way. “If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth”. We have to remember Jerusalem: our works in this earth, and why God keeps bringing us back in this earth. If you do not remember Jerusalem, there is no need for you to say anything; your mouth cannot prophesy anything.

“If I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy.” When we see Jerusalem as our chief joy, we will show up on the feast days among the brothers, because those are the joyful days, the glad of heart days. Esau gave you the day off on his national holiday, and the school was empty. The same zeal we have for the sabbath we have to have for the feast days and new moons.

It is a comfort to see brothers and sisters in the same fight: a sister who has to work at seven stays among the sisters till late because she loves her people. Some of you take Jerusalem as bitterness: every sabbath again, every new moon again. That is not joy in God. We have to prefer Jerusalem above everything.

sense.text: “Give testimony unto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in thy name.” Raise up prophets, not weak men: prophets taught in his name. These brothers are going to keep it pushing; they will take the work seriously and constantly endure. That is why we are not going to forget the joy.

“Reward them that wait for thee”. God is going to reward them that wait upon him. We are not telling you to take vengeance on the enemy, because vengeance is of the Lord. We leave it in the hands of God, but one thing we know: judgment is coming for this place.

precepts.why: “He that revengeth shall find vengeance from the Lord”. We are supposed to understand that among our own people, and so with the enemy, because the Lord said vengeance belongs to him. That is why we wait for him, and he rewards them that wait.

sense.text:
This scripture is for the brother who thinks he can go and harm the enemy: you will go to jail, or they will not even give you the time for jail; they will kill you in the street. Don't be simple. Wait patiently.

“Therefore wait ye upon me, saith the Lord”. That is what God said we must do: wait upon him, “until the day that I rise up to the prey”.

precepts.why:
“For thy power standeth not in multitude nor thy might in strong men”. God's power does not stand in multitude, nor his might in strong men. “For thou art a God of the afflicted”: are we not afflicted? So he is our God. “An helper of the oppressed”: are we not oppressed? “An upholder of the weak”: are we not weak in this flesh? “A protector of the forlorn”: do we not need protection? So he is our protector.

“A saviour of them that are without hope.” We cannot hope in this place; we have to hope upon God. The power of hope is for us to hope upon God, because he is our strength when we are weak, our protector when we need protection, the one we need when we are oppressed and afflicted. Let us put our trust in him, and our hope in him.

“And make every nation and tribe to acknowledge that thou art the God of all power and might”. He is the God of all power, and of might. “And that there is none other that protecteth the people of Israel but thou.” There is no other God in this earth. The white man is no God; he is given a time right now, but he is a man. There is none other that protects us but God.

This is the day God rises up to the prey. “Woe to the nations that rise up against my kindred!” Woe and destruction to every nation that rises up against the nation of Israel. We have been slaves under every nation on the planet: under the Assyrian, under Babylon, under the Medes and Persians, under the Greek and Rome, and now under America. America is not the last; all these nations must be checked.

“The Lord Almighty will take vengeance of them in the day of judgment”. So should we go out and decide to go against our enemy? That is not what we just read.

“In putting fire and worms in their flesh; and they shall feel them, and weep for ever.” That is their judgment: they are going to burn up. That is what we hope for. We cannot burn this nation, but God can: our King, our power, our protector.

sense.text: “It is good that a man should both hope”. God said it is good that a man hope: that is the power of hope. “And quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.” Quietly, brothers and sisters, we wait for the salvation of God's people, which is us. It is good that we hope for the salvation of our people. Don't be a fool out here.

precepts.why:
“But let us, who are of the day, be sober”: be sober, be alert, “putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation.” We must put the helmet on for the hope of our salvation; that is why we are covered by the law, the statutes and the commandments.

“For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ”. Our salvation is going to come from Christ himself, so what are you worried about? Be patient and endure; your time will come, for the oppression, the affliction, the rape and murder they have done to us.

All these precepts mean nothing if you do not take control of your own mind. Your mind makes it real: everything around us was once a thought. If you are not controlling your mind, somebody else is controlling it. That is why we have to wait upon the Lord.

“For my hope is in the Everlasting, that he will save you”. Our hope is supposed to be in the Everlasting. “And joy is come unto me from the Holy One, because of the mercy which shall soon come unto you from the Everlasting our Saviour.”

sense.text: “In hope of eternal life”. Our hope, brothers and sisters, is to have eternal life, “which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began”. With all the oppression and all the affliction, God promised it before the world began, and God cannot turn around and say he will not give it: he is God, and he can never lie. He promised us before the world began eternal life, the new body. We must control the mind.

precepts.why: “Order my steps in thy word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me.” That is what we have to pray for. That is why we have to take full control of our mind: that is where our sin comes from, and where its dominion comes from, holding us down when we are captive to our sin. We pray that the Lord guides our steps in his word; that is the only way we are going to be protected and keep hold of the hope of eternal life.
